concepts.name: ThreadPoolExecutor
concepts.description: ThreadPoolExecutor runs callables concurrently in a pool of OS threads and is commonly useful for overlapping blocking I/O.

concepts.name: ProcessPoolExecutor
concepts.description: ProcessPoolExecutor runs work in separate processes, allowing CPU-bound Python code to use multiple cores.

concepts.name: concurrent.futures.as_completed
concepts.description: as_completed(futures) yields Future objects as each finishes, which is useful when processing results in completion order instead of submission order.

concepts.name: threading.Event
concepts.description: threading.Event is a thread-safe flag used to signal one or many waiting threads that a condition has occurred.

concepts.name: threading.Lock
concepts.description: threading.Lock provides mutual exclusion between threads; a with lock: block acquires and releases it safely.

concepts.name: queue.Queue for threads
concepts.description: queue.Queue is a synchronized producer-consumer queue for threads and supports blocking put/get plus task_done/join tracking.

concepts.name: Explicit multiprocessing start context
concepts.description: multiprocessing.get_context(name) lets code explicitly choose a process start method instead of depending on a platform/version default.

questions.prompt: Submit each blocking fetch to the existing thread pool.

content.template:
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
    futures = [{{answer}} for url in urls]

questions.explanation: ThreadPoolExecutor runs callables concurrently in a pool of OS threads and is commonly useful for overlapping blocking I/O. with ThreadPoolExecutor() as pool: futures = [pool.submit(fetch, url) for url in urls] submits independent calls. questions.prompt: Stop the worker loop when another thread signals the event.
questions.explanation: threading.Event is a thread-safe flag used to signal one or many waiting threads that a condition has occurred. worker loops often use while not stop_event.is_set(): ... and another thread calls stop_event.set(). Event is signaling, not mutual exclusion; use Lock when shared mutable state itself needs serialized access.

questions.prompt: Use the existing thread lock around the shared update.
questions.explanation: threading.Lock provides mutual exclusion between threads; a with lock: block acquires and releases it safely. Use with lock: around the smallest shared-state critical section that must be atomic across threads. A Lock does not make compound operations automatically atomic unless those operations actually run while the lock is held.

questions.prompt: Explicitly request spawn semantics instead of relying on the platform default.
questions.explanation: multiprocessing.get_context(name) lets code explicitly choose a process start method instead of depending on a platform/version default. ctx = multiprocessing.get_context('spawn') can be passed to APIs that accept an mp_context. Start-method defaults differ across platforms and changed again on POSIX in Python 3.14, so code requiring a specific method should request it explicitly.
